title: Sound-Alike Words
kidRule: Some words sound exactly the same but have different spellings and different meanings. Think about what the word means, and the meaning will usually help you choose the spelling!
hint: Careful! This word has a sound-alike twin. Listen to the sentence again. Which meaning do we need?
reminder: Sound-alike words are spelled by their meaning. Picture what this word means and use the spelling that goes with that meaning.

check.question: Why is PIECE spelled with P-I-E at the start?
check.correctAnswer: Because it is the one that means a part of something, like a PIECE of PIE!
distractors: Because every word that sounds the same is spelled the same way
Because I and E always come before the letter C

words.sent: May I have a piece of your birthday cake?
words.story: The first jigsaw puzzles were maps cut into pieces to help children learn where countries are!
words.card: I ate a *piece* of *pie* as big as my head!

words.def: All of something, with nothing missing.
words.sent: She read the whole book in one afternoon.
words.story: A snake swallows its food whole because it cannot chew!
words.card: *Who* ate the *whole* cake? The frosting on the dog's nose is a clue!

words.def: Noticed a sound with your ears a little while ago.
words.sent: We heard thunder rumbling far away.
words.story: The deep songs of some whales can be heard by other whales many miles away!
words.card: I *heard* a tiny burp, and my *ear* says it was the goldfish!

words.def: Someone who is invited to visit or to come to a party.
words.sent: Each guest got a balloon at the party.
words.story: In Sweden there is a hotel made of ice and snow that is rebuilt every winter. Each guest sleeps on a bed of ice!
words.card: Every *guest* got a *gu*mmy worm and a paper crown!

words.def: What the sky and air are like outside, such as sunny, rainy, windy, or snowy.
words.sent: The weather was perfect for flying a kite.
words.story: The weather can be wild. A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun!
words.card: We *eat* popsicles in any *weather*, even when it snows!

words.def: Let someone do something, or said that it is okay.
words.sent: We are allowed to stay up late on Fridays.
words.story: At many libraries, kids are allowed to read stories to friendly dogs. The dogs love it, and it is great reading practice!
words.card: 'Are giraffes *allowed* to fly this *low*?' asked the pilot!

words.def: To take something that is not yours.
words.sent: The sneaky raccoon tried to steal our sandwiches.
words.story: Seagulls at the beach sometimes steal snacks right out of people's hands!
words.card: Who would *steal* my cup of *tea*? The teddy bear looks guilty!

words.def: To stop for a short time before going on.
words.sent: Please pause the movie while I get a snack.
words.story: In music, a moment when nobody plays is called a rest, and it has its own special symbols!
words.card: *Use* the remote to *pause* the cartoon before the pie lands!

words.def: A breakfast food made from grains, usually eaten in a bowl with milk.
words.sent: I poured milk over my crunchy cereal.
words.story: The word comes from Ceres, the Roman goddess of grain and farming!
words.card: Is that a *real* dragon eating my *cereal*?

words.def: The person in charge of a school.
words.sent: The principal read a story to our class.
words.story: Long ago, the head of a school was called the 'principal teacher', which meant the main teacher. Over time, people dropped the second word!
words.card: The *principal* is my *pal*, and she wears roller skates on Fridays!
